_comment: Storyboard for the unit lecture film of Repair a Dripping Tap (Professor Adow TVET, Home Repair, lesson 2). Scoped deliberately: the owner's source document covers seven faucet types across nine pages, and this film does ONE job end to end — the washer (compression) tap — because that is the one the document details fully and the one a learner will actually meet. Washerless types appear only in the identify scene, so a learner knows when this procedure does NOT apply. Every art.at key must appear VERBATIM in its beat's say. UK / East African terms: tap, spout, gland nut, gland packing.
title: Repair a Dripping Tap
subtitle: Home Repair
_voice: Daniel. The school's voice, owner's choice 2026-09-24.

brand.name: Professor Adow TVET
brand.by: A short unit lecture from Professor Adow TVET

objectives: Identify a washer (compression) tap against a washerless one.
Isolate the supply at the correct point and prove it.
Strip a compression tap in order without marking it.
Tell a drip at the spout from a weep at the stem.
Replace the washer and its brass screw, matched.
Judge whether the seat is renewable or must be dressed.
Renew the gland packing or the stem O-ring.
Reassemble in reverse, greased, hand tight plus a half turn.

beats.say: A tap that drips is not about to fail. It has already failed, and every drop is going down the drain paid for. Closing it harder stops the noise for a day and drives the damage deeper into the tap.
Decide that before you touch a spanner. A washer tap screws down: the handle turns several times and it closes by pressing rubber onto brass. That is the tap this film repairs.

A washerless tap moves a quarter turn, or is a single lever, and inside it is a cartridge, a disc pack or a ball. It has no washer to change, so this procedure does not apply and you fit a kit instead.
Turn the water off at the service valve under the fitting if there is one, and at the main stop tap if there is not. Shut the hot supply at the heater as well.
Then open the tap and let it run dry. That is not a formality. It is the only proof you have shut the right valve, and it costs you ten seconds against a room full of water.
Look at where the water is coming from, because there are two faults and they are not the same. Water from the spout is the washer or the seat: the tap is not closing.
Water around the handle is a weep at the stem, and that is the gland packing or the O-ring. Strip a tap for the wrong one and you will fit a new washer to a fault that was never there.

at.wrong: Strip a tap for the wrong one

beats.say: Prise or unscrew the cap in the middle of the handle. Under it is one screw. Take it out, and the handle lifts off the stem. If it is stuck, put the screw back a couple of turns and pull against that.
Now slacken the gland nut and thread the whole stem out by turning it in the OPEN direction. Pad your plier jaws with tape before they touch chrome, and go gently on plastic.
On the end of the stem is the washer, held by a brass screw. A washer that has gone hard, or has a groove pressed into it, is your drip. Undo the screw and take the old one off.

at.groove: has a groove pressed into it

beats.say: Take the old washer with you and match it for size and style. Guessing gets you one that almost fits, which leaks. If the brass screw is chewed, renew that too, in brass and not in steel.
If this tap eats washers every few months, the washer is not the fault. The seat is: the brass ring the washer closes onto has been cut, and it is cutting each new washer in turn.

Shine a torch down the body. A square, hexagonal or slotted hole means the seat unscrews, and a seat wrench turns it out anticlockwise. A plain round hole means it does not, and you dress it in place until it is smooth.

at.square: A square, hexagonal or slotted hole

beats.say: For the other fault, renew the gland packing. Wrap one turn around the stem under the nut, in the direction the nut tightens, so that doing the nut up winds the packing in rather than unwinding it. Some stems take an O-ring instead: match it and fit it.

at.direction: in the direction the nut tightens

beats.say: Back together in the reverse order of taking it apart, with a smear of silicone grease on the stem threads so the handle turns sweetly.

The gland nut goes hand tight and then half a turn more. Not as hard as it will go: over-tighten it and the handle becomes stiff and the packing is crushed. Turn the water back on slowly and watch both places before you walk away.

So: identify the kind. Isolate, and prove it dry. Read which leak it is. Strip it in order, padded. Washer and seat for a spout drip, packing for a stem weep. Then reverse, greased, hand tight and a half turn.
